items.heading: A Zoology Degree
items.text: A zoology degree is a ladder with different jobs on each rung. The BSc opens few doors by itself.

items.heading: Pay Lines Mean Little Without
items.text: Pay lines mean little without the fee and the contract length beside them. This ledger uses notices and official pages, and it leaves out the unsourced ranges that most career blogs print.

rows: Lab and project assistant posts, B.Ed and school teaching, state and central exams that name the subject, MSc entry. A 2024 Central Silk Board institute project notice, as reported, listed Zoology among accepted BSc subjects, but it was a contract post tied to one project.
One applied skill: fish or bee farming basics, GIS, statistics or a lab method. Plus one field or lab log you can show.
Not so scalable on the degree alone. Scalable with a business layer when you add a farm, lab or teaching business.
Project fellow and research biologist posts at conservation bodies, ZSI and university projects, PGT teaching, NET and JRF entry.
Field survey method, data analysis in R or Python, report writing, and one species or habitat you know deeply.
Not so scalable as a salaried researcher. Scalable with a business layer through consulting, testing or training.
Scientist, faculty and senior research posts, if a post is open. A fellowship is training, not a job.
Papers, a funded project, supervision record and a skill that works outside academia.
Not so scalable. Several filters stack up, so keep an industry or consulting skill running.

items.heading: Pick Two Routes, Not Seven
items.text: Pick two routes, not seven. Run both through the four questions and set the rest aside.

items.heading: Open the Real Notice
items.text: Open the real notice for each. Read the qualification, age and pay lines on the official page or advertisement, not a blog summary.

items.heading: Do One Small Piece
items.text: Do one small piece of work in each. A local species survey, a pond visit with a farmer, a recorded explainer, or a small analysis of a public dataset. Go at your own pace.

items.heading: Ask Three People Who Do
items.text: Ask three people who do the work. One from each route and one who left it. Ask what the first year felt like and what they earned.

figures.label: Growth Rate
figures.source: India is the second-largest fish producer, about 8 percent of world output. Production rose from 96 lakh tonnes in 2013-14 to 195 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, and the sector supports over 30 million livelihoods (PIB, 20 November 2025). Many fisheries posts and the ICAR master's route are written around fisheries degrees, so check whether a zoology MSc qualifies before you plan on a salaried post.
